source.filename: 2024-Modeling of Stick-Slip Contact Mechanics Based on Improved Continuous-Scale Fractal-Discrete Iwan Model.pdf

constitutive_assumptions: Rough surface contact is equivalent to contact between a rigid flat plane and a rough surface.
Single asperity contact profile is simplified using a two-dimensional cosine profile according to the Majumdar-Bhushan (MB) model.
Deformation of individual asperities follows the Chang-Etsion-Bogy (CEB) model with discrete fully elastic and fully plastic regimes, neglecting intermediate elastoplastic transition states.
There is no mutual mechanical interaction among individual micro-asperities across the contact surface.
Normal contact forces distributed among individual micro-asperities (Jenkins units) follow a geometric series distribution.
All individual discrete Jenkins units possess identical tangential spring stiffness.
At any given scale, the number distribution of asperities is assumed uniform across different contact areas.
Surface topography and fractal parameters remain unchanged during sliding and cyclic tangential loading.
Unloading and reloading tangential force-displacement relationships follow Masing's mapping rule.
control_variables: Material properties of the contact pair (No. 45 steel: elastic modulus E = 209 GPa, Poisson's ratio ν = 0.27, hardness H = 157 MPa)
Number of Jenkins elements in the discrete Iwan model (empirically determined from total normal force and maximum contact force)
Minimum asperity length scale (set by measurement instrument resolution)
dependent_variables: Real contact area and contact area ratio (Ar, A/Ar)
Normal contact stiffness and dimensionless normal stiffness (Ke, Kp, K*)
Total normal force (Fn) and maximum contact spot area (aL)
Tangential force (Fτ) and tangential shear stress (τ)
Tangential hysteresis loop shape and energy dissipation area

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Classical MB-based contact models assume complete deformation for all asperities with a constant global critical contact area, causing calculation deviations for small contact areas and failing to capture the elastic-to-plastic temporal evolution of individual asperities.
Introducing asperity length scale and contact area as two independent variables yields a scale-dependent critical area expression and a continuous-scale asperity number distribution function.
Normal contact stiffness increases with normal load and fractal dimension D, but decreases with increasing fractal roughness G, exhibiting a local peak across roughness ranges.
Tangential stick-slip response exhibits tangential stiffness softening in the micro-slip regime followed by constant residual stiffness during macroscopic sliding.
Increasing normal load and friction coefficient shifts the macroscopic sliding onset to larger tangential displacements and linearly increases the macro-slip tangential force.
The improved fractal-discrete Iwan model demonstrates agreement with literature experimental hysteresis loops for steel specimens under normal loads between 200 N and 600 N.

experimental_setup: Validation was conducted against benchmark experimental data from secondary literature (Zong et al., 2022).
Specimens were sliding blocks of No. 45 steel with elastic modulus of 209 GPa, Poisson's ratio of 0.27, and hardness of 157 MPa.
Three rough surface slider profiles were evaluated: Slider 1 (D = 1.54, G = 3.99e-9 m), Slider 2 (D = 1.47, G = 4.44e-8 m), and Slider 3 (D = 1.43, G = 4.71e-8 m).
Normal loads were applied in the range of 200 N to 600 N (specifically around 203 N–208 N, 404 N–406 N, and 606 N–608 N).
Cyclic tangential displacement loading was applied with amplitudes between 60 μm and 100 μm.
future_work: Replacing the constant macroscopic friction coefficient with local, fractal-described friction coefficients for individual micro-contacts to enhance physical fidelity.
Developing theoretical or physics-based formulations for initial tangential stiffness to eliminate reliance on empirical parameter identification.
Applying the stick-slip contact formulation in structural finite element simulations of mechanical assembly interfaces.
independent_variables: Tangential displacement and cyclic displacement amplitude (x, xmax)
limitations_inferred: The model was validated solely on metallic (No. 45 steel) contact interfaces from literature and was not demonstrated on soft, elastomeric, hyperelastic, or viscoelastic materials common in soft robotics.
The fractal contact formulation assumes two-dimensional profile representations extended isotropically, without accounting for surface texture anisotropy or directional lay.
Dynamic inertia, rate dependence, and frictional thermal effects during continuous high-frequency stick-slip cycles are not incorporated.
Loading is restricted to unidirectional tangential shear coupled with normal compression, omitting multi-axial bending or torsional interfacial loading.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Neighboring asperities on the contact interface are assumed to have no mutual interaction.
Wear and morphological evolution of the surface topography during sliding are not considered.
Initial tangential stiffness in the discrete Iwan formulation relies on experimental parameter identification rather than direct physical derivation, weakening physical interpretability.
A uniform macroscopic friction coefficient is assumed rather than localized micro-contact friction coefficients.
The single-asperity CEB formulation assumes an abrupt transition between fully elastic and fully plastic states, omitting intermediate elastoplastic phases.
main_results: The continuous-scale fractal model resolves the inconsistency of classical MB models regarding plastic deformation of small asperities by establishing that asperities deform elastically before plastic yield.

Dimensionless normal contact stiffness rises monotonically with normal load and fractal dimension D, but decreases with fractal roughness G, showing a distinct peak across certain roughness ranges that shifts toward higher roughness as D increases.
Normal stiffness derived from the CEB-based continuous-scale model exhibits a quadratic-like growth curve with normal force compared to the more linear progression seen in KE-based models.
Tangential hysteresis curves display two distinct stages: stiffness degradation during micro-slip and stable residual stiffness during macro-slip.
Higher normal loads and friction coefficients delay the onset of macro-slip to larger tangential displacements and scale the saturation sliding force linearly.
Simulated hysteresis loops from the coupled continuous-scale fractal and discrete Iwan model show close alignment with experimental data across different surface topographies and normal load levels.
modeling_methods: Continuous-scale fractal surface representation based on Morag-Etsion (ME) and Weierstrass-Mandelbrot (W-M) theories.
Chang-Etsion-Bogy (CEB) single-asperity contact model defining elastic-fully plastic transitions.
Two-variable continuous-scale asperity distribution function n'(a, l) dependent on asperity scale and contact spot area.
Discrete Iwan stick-slip model with parallel Jenkins elements and geometric-series normal load distribution.
Masing mapping rule for predicting cyclic tangential force-displacement hysteresis loops during unloading and reloading.
performance_metrics: Dimensionless normal contact stiffness (K*) versus dimensionless normal load (Fn*)
Relative area proportion of micro-contacts smaller than a specified area (A/Ar versus a/aL)
Tangential force-displacement hysteresis curve profile and enclosed loop area (frictional energy dissipation)
Correlation between theoretical hysteresis loops and experimental measurements
possible_gap_implications: The continuous-scale formulation mitigates scale-truncation errors for small contact interfaces in numerical structural assembly simulations, but adapting it to soft robotics would require reformulating asperity mechanics for large-deformation hyperelastic and viscoelastic polymers.
paper.research_objective: To establish an improved continuous-scale fractal and discrete Iwan stick-slip contact mechanics model by introducing asperity length scale and contact spot area as independent variables, deriving a scale-dependent critical area and asperity distribution function, and characterizing interfacial tangential hysteresis under combined normal and tangential loading.
paper.research_problem: Existing Majumdar-Bhushan (MB) based fractal-Iwan coupling models assume that all micro-asperities undergo complete deformation and share a globally constant elastoplastic critical area, leading to calculation deviations for normal forces on small contact spots and rendering the model incompatible with small nominal contact areas in structural assembly simulations.
paper.title: 改进的连续尺度分形−离散Iwan 黏滑接触力学建模 (Modeling of Stick-Slip Contact Mechanics Based on Improved Continuous-Scale Fractal-Discrete Iwan Model)
